sourceSection: §3.1 Primary Efficacy — Culture Conversion at Month 6
sourcePassage: Culture conversion at month 6 was 92.3% (95% CI 89.4–94.5) in the 9-month levofloxacin arm versus 91.8% (95% CI 88.8–94.1) in the 12-month standard arm — an absolute difference of +0.5 percentage points (95% CI −3.1 to +4.2), meeting the pre-specified non-inferiority margin of 5 percentage points.

sourcePassage: MRI-confirmed radiological healing (Bhojraj grade ≥ III) was achieved in 87.4% (9-month arm) versus 88.1% (12-month arm) at 24 months — consistent with the culture-conversion result and supporting durable structural recovery under the shortened regimen.

title: Shorter Regimen — Adherence & Programme Cost Benefit

sourcePassage: Spinal tuberculosis (Pott's disease) is a form of TB that affects the vertebrae — the bones in your spine. It causes back pain, stiffness, and if untreated, can damage the spinal cord. It is treatable with a combination of TB medicines taken for several months.
title: What is Spine TB? — Patient Explainer

sourcePassage: Completing the full course of TB medicines is essential for cure and to prevent drug-resistant TB. A 9-month course is shorter than the standard 12-month course — this may make it easier for people to complete their treatment.
title: Why Completing Treatment Matters — Patient Adherence
